name: issue_645_restart_debounce_bypass_open_window
description: A restart/redeploy makes a monitored group/helper contact sensor blip unavailable->on, stamping a fresh last_changed on a window that has physically been open for hours. _sensor_debounce_pending() must not read that reconnect blip as a fresh open -- it must never let the Issue #629 choke-point guard in _apply_comfort_band() arm an active HVAC mode through the still-open window (Issue #645).
notes: Occupant impact: after a redeploy, the dashboard showed Status 'windows open (as planned)'
and Doors/Windows '1 open' (both correct) but HVAC flipped to 'cool, 74F' with indoor at
69F. hvac_action stayed idle this time (indoor was well below the setpoint) so no energy
was wasted on this occurrence, but the automation commanded cool mode through an open
window without its safety check running -- on a warmer morning the identical race would
let the compressor actually engage.
Root cause (five whys, confirmed via live production logs and REST state history):
apply_classification()'s regular cycle reached _apply_comfort_band(), whose Issue #629
choke-point guard requires `not self._sensor_debounce_pending` before it will pause on an
open sensor. _sensor_debounce_pending() was True because the monitored contact-sensor
group entity's last_changed was recent -- NOT because the door had just opened, but
because the entity itself blipped 'unavailable -> on' during HA startup (confirmed via
`tools/ha_logs.py --history`: binary_sensor.group_contact_sensors_climate_advisor
transitioned unavailable->on at 07:54:53->07:56:05 local, precisely bracketing the
07:55:00 redeploy), even though the door had been open continuously since well before
06:00 that morning.
First fix attempt (reverted during this same investigation): dropping the
`not self._sensor_debounce_pending` clause entirely from the arm-blocking guards. This
broke the golden scenario issue_623_debounce_race_transient_open_not_paused -- debounce
exists precisely to avoid an instant pause when a user BRIEFLY opens a door (a genuine
off->on transition), and blanket-removing the check would reintroduce nuisance-pause
regressions. The real fix needed to distinguish a genuine transition from a reconnect blip,
not discard the protection wholesale.
Actual fix: coordinator._async_door_window_changed() now inspects old_state when a
monitored sensor reads open. If old_state.state is 'unavailable'/'unknown' (a reconnect,
not a real transition), it records that specific last_changed value in the new
_sensor_reconnect_blip_last_changed dict and skips debounce-timer registration entirely --
it does NOT treat old_state=None the same way (only unavailable/unknown are confirmed blip
signatures; a genuine first-ever open should still debounce normally).
_sensor_debounce_pending()'s last_changed fallback (Issue #623) now excludes any
last_changed value recorded as a known blip for that sensor -- a LATER genuine off->on
transition moves last_changed again, so this exclusion can never mask a real open. The
arm-blocking guards in automation.py (_apply_comfort_band(), Issue #629;
_sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors(), Issue #620) are UNCHANGED -- their existing
`not self._sensor_debounce_pending` check now simply evaluates correctly for a reconnect
blip, because the underlying signal it reads is now correct.
Harness fidelity fix (also this PR): simulate_restart previously only called
engine.restore_state(engine.get_serializable_state()), which leaves _paused_by_door/
_pre_pause_mode/_natural_vent_active untouched by design (restore_state()'s own docstring:
relies on a fresh __init__ having already zeroed them, since production constructs a new
engine instance on every real restart). Because the harness reuses the SAME live engine
object across simulate_restart, those fields silently leaked across the simulated
restart -- masking exactly the class of post-restart bug this event type exists to
reproduce, discovered while authoring this scenario. simulate_restart now also explicitly
resets those fields to their __init__ defaults, matching the real clean-slate guarantee.
Scenario design: the window is opened via a genuine sensor_open (real off->on transition,
registers a normal debounce timer) well before the redeploy, then the debounce window is
allowed to fully elapse (via a later temp_update) so it is genuinely settled going into the
restart -- matching the real incident (open since well before 06:00, long-settled).
simulate_restart models the redeploy using the real production continuity boundary (Issue
#627's event). sensor_unavailable (new Issue #645 event type) then sets the SAME entity to
'unavailable' with no listener dispatch, followed by a plain sensor_open that fires the
real _async_door_window_changed() listener with old_state.state=='unavailable' --
faithfully reproducing the confirmed live REST history mechanism (unavailable->on during
startup), not a guess. The following classification (windows_recommended=true,
hvac_mode=off, matching the real incident's planned-window classification) must not arm
cool.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting the Issue #645 fix in coordinator.py (removing the
old_state check from _async_door_window_changed()/the exclusion from
_sensor_debounce_pending()) makes this scenario fail -- the post-restart classification
cycle would see debounce_pending=True (unexcluded fresh last_changed from the
reconnect) and arm hvac_mode=cool via set_temperature, exactly reproducing the
incident. Verified via revert-test on tests/test_sensor_reconnect_blip.py and this
scenario before promoting. issue_623_debounce_race_transient_open_not_paused (a
genuine transient-open scenario) continues to pass unmodified with this fix, verifying
the fix is scoped to reconnect blips only.
(b) Docs-production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's door/window section is
updated in this same PR to note the reconnect-blip exclusion fixed here, alongside
the #620/#623/#629 entries.
(c) User outcome: a redeploy/restart no longer creates a ~10-minute window where the
automation can silently command active HVAC mode through a monitored window that has
been open for hours -- the dashboard's 'windows open' status and the actual HVAC
behavior stay consistent across every restart, not just in steady state -- while a
user briefly stepping through a monitored door still gets the debounce protection
Issue #623 established.

events.note: Well before the redeploy: matches the real incident's conditions.

Genuine off->on transition -- fires the real _async_door_window_changed() listener, registers a normal 600s debounce timer (matches Issue #623's protection: a real open must still debounce). This (and the morning wakeup at 06:30) may set _paused_by_door=True and/or _natural_vent_active=True pre-restart -- simulate_restart below now explicitly resets both (see its Issue #645 note) to match the real clean-slate guarantee a fresh engine instance provides in production.
15 minutes later -- the 600s debounce window has long since elapsed, so the sensor is genuinely settled-open going into the restart below, matching the real incident (open since well before 06:00).

Models the redeploy/restart (matches the real incident's 07:55:00 v0.6.17 startup). restore_state(get_serializable_state()) clean-slate wipes engine flags; coordinator._startup_coalesce_active resets to True, its real post-restart default.

Silently sets the entity to 'unavailable' (no listener dispatch) -- models the underlying platform/group entity losing connectivity during the HA restart, setting up old_state for the reconnect event below.

The SAME already-open sensor re-reports 'on', firing the real _async_door_window_changed() listener with old_state.state=='unavailable' -- matches the confirmed live REST history: unavailable->on at 07:54:53->07:56:05 local, bracketing the redeploy. This is the exact reconnect-blip mechanism Issue #645 fixes.

The post-coalescing regular-cycle classification that mis-armed cool mode in production (matches the real incident's 08:00:11.205 log entry). Without the fix, debounce_pending reads True (last_changed only 4m6s old from the reconnect blip) -- the Issue #629 choke-point guard in _apply_comfort_band() is the only thing standing between this cycle and the open window, and it was defeated by the unexcluded reconnect timestamp.

assertions.reason: Issue #645: the post-restart comfort-band arm must never command 'cool' (or 'heat') mode -- neither via set_hvac_mode nor via set_temperature's bundled hvac_mode parameter (the actual mechanism that fired in production) -- through a window that is genuinely open, even when a restart-caused reconnect blip stamps a fresh last_changed.

The Issue #629 choke-point guard in _apply_comfort_band() must set _paused_by_door=True when it refuses to arm through the open window -- now correctly evaluating _sensor_debounce_pending()=False once the reconnect-blip last_changed is excluded, so the pause is visible on the Status card and subsequent cycles correctly stay gated via decide_scheduled_band_gate()'s DEFER_PAUSED.

verdict.summary: A restart/redeploy that stamps a fresh last_changed on an already-open monitored sensor via a reconnect blip no longer bypasses the open-window HVAC-arm guard (Issue #645)
verdict.observed_behavior: genuine open + full debounce settle pre-restart -> simulate_restart -> unavailable/on reconnect blip on the same sensor -> post-coalescing classification cycle -> comfort-band arm is intercepted by the choke-point guard because the reconnect blip is correctly excluded from debounce_pending, HVAC stays off, _paused_by_door=True
verdict.expected_behavior: No active HVAC mode is ever commanded while a monitored window remains genuinely open, across any restart timing -- while a genuine brief transient open (Issue #623) still correctly debounces
